scope.sample: Six purposively selected captured source URLs, with one verbatim captured claim selected per source.
scope.method: Read source pages and relevant sections through web retrieval. Follow the arXiv full text and, for one inaccessible cited URL, identify related primary-origin material. Separate URL access, claim support and source role.
not_tested: Commercial score accuracy or actual tool results
The raw calculations or reproducibility of cited studies
Independent human agreement with assistant coding

items.claim_excerpt: For ChatGPT search eligibility, OpenAI specifically recommends allowing `OAI-SearchBot`; inclusion or placement is still not guaranteed.

access.method: Read public source with web retrieval open/find; no sign-in, product execution or paid API request.
access.evidence: Readable official help article. The website-eligibility section states that the crawler and its published traffic must be allowed; the preceding sentence disclaims guaranteed placement.

support.rationale: The eligibility advice and non-guarantee are present. This is documentation support for the selected claim, not a crawl test of a real product site or proof that allowing a bot increases recommendations.

source_role.qualification: Official OpenAI help; current text checked after collection. Other claims in the answer, including cross-platform behavior, were not checked.

items.evidence_locator: Make your website available in search results

items.claim_excerpt: xAI’s own evaluation guidance warns that model judges can exhibit position bias, favor longer answers, and drift from human judgment.

access.method: Read public source with web retrieval open/find; no sign-in, product execution or paid API request.
access.evidence: Readable official best-practices page. Its grader table lists the three risks; the next paragraph recommends rubrics, randomized order and comparison with human labels.

support.rationale: The selected warning is directly supported. It does not supply a measured error rate for this experiment or establish that assistant coding agrees with a person.

source_role.qualification: Provider guidance, not independent validation of Stage 3 coding. Genuine human review remains pending.

items.short_source_quote: Position bias, preference for longer answers, drift from human judgment
items.evidence_locator: Evaluate Grok models / Design the eval

items.claim_excerpt: LLM evaluations can vary across repeated runs and small wording changes, so aggregate rankings without uncertainty can look more definitive than they are.

access.method: Read public source with web retrieval open/find; no sign-in, product execution or paid API request.
access.evidence: Abstract and full text were readable. Limitations excludes linguistic-variation analysis; experiments concern repeated spatial-reasoning tests.

support.rationale: Supports repeat uncertainty, not the wording-change clause: linguistic variation was explicitly untested. GEO metrics were not evaluated.

source_role.qualification: Original spatial-reasoning methods preprint; peer review and replication were not established.

items.short_source_quote: We have not looked at the impact of linguistic variation
items.material_caution: Partial sentence support; original coding remains unchanged.

items.claim_excerpt: SparkToro research (nearly 3,000 runs across ChatGPT, Claude, and Google AI) found less than a 1-in-100 chance of identical brand lists and roughly 1-in-1,000 for the same list in the same order.

access.method: Read public source with web retrieval open/find; no sign-in, product execution or paid API request.
access.evidence: Readable original research post. It reports 2,961 volunteer runs across three services, approximate list/order repetition statements, and a collaboration with Gumshoe.

support.rationale: The attributed study and approximations are present. The text gives a slightly different qualification for Claude, and Grok was not tested. Statistical calculations, raw responses and population-level probabilities were not independently reproduced.

source_role.qualification: Original commercial research collaboration with disclosed interests; not an independent audit of all visibility vendors or of Stage 3. This is support that the authors reported the results, not validation of universal rates.

items.evidence_locator: Experiment setup, list/order variability and stated limitations
items.commercial_provenance: SparkToro study with a Gumshoe collaborator; interests disclosed in the article.

items.claim_excerpt: Ahrefs free AI Visibility Checker (brand name in → mentions across several engines, top topics/domains)

access.method: Read public source with web retrieval open/find; no sign-in, product execution or paid API request.
access.evidence: The supplied path redirected to the Ahrefs AI Visibility Checker page. The readable vendor page describes brand-name input, multi-platform mentions, topics and cited domains.

support.rationale: The named product and described report features are advertised. No query was submitted, no account or payment was used, and no score accuracy, plan entitlement or free-price claim was tested. The listed platforms do not establish Grok coverage.

source_role.qualification: First-party product description, not an independently validated measurement method. The captured recommendation remains an observed model recommendation.

items.evidence_locator: How to check your brand’s AI visibility / What’s in your report

items.claim_excerpt: One 2026 benchmark found average top-five shortlist overlap of about 43% when the *same* engine answered the same questions again, and only ~17% *across* engines.

access.method: Read public source with web retrieval open/find; no sign-in, product execution or paid API request.
access.evidence: The exact Markets URL returned a tool access error, without a verifiable HTTP status. A same-title originating Crackle PR release on GlobeNewswire and the agency’s methodology page were readable.

support.rationale: The originating release reports the selected figures for a 500-answer, four-API B2B PR benchmark and defines overlap as Jaccard. This does not verify the inaccessible Markets copy, reproduce the calculations or generalize to consumer interfaces.

source_role.reviewed: First-party agency research press release; exact Markets copy unavailable
source_role.qualification: The readable origin is a commercially interested agency’s release, not independent editorial research. The original Markets category needs a qualification; exact syndication identity was not authenticated. No original category is silently overwritten.

items.evidence_locator: Originating release: experiment description and Scope and Limits; agency methodology: actual collection

related_primary_sources.role: Originating release; labelled Source: Crackle PR

items.material_caution: Do not treat the host name or a syndicated release as proof of independent editorial provenance. The inaccessible exact URL remains unverified.

material_findings: The arXiv citation supports repeated-run uncertainty, but not the accompanying wording-change claim.
The inaccessible Markets citation has a readable commercial press-release origin. Keep exact-URL unavailability and editorial-provenance qualification visible.
summary.interpretation: A supported attribution or feature description is narrower than an independently verified empirical claim. These checks do not validate every source or replace actual human review.
